messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> redis-acceptqueue-high (P1) for service: redis-cluster-west-1. Trigger: accept_queue_length > 500 on replica nodes.

pagerduty: Incident: PD-87421 triggered by monitor: redis-acceptqueue-high. Paging: Emma (primary oncall).

Emma: acked. I'm taking it. Looking at dashboards now. :eyes:

prod-monitor-bot: Metrics snapshot: replicas: [r1,r2,r3], avg_accept_queue: 612, max_clients: 10240, blocked_clients: 72, client_output_buffer_limit_hit: 8. 90th latency (ops): 1.8s -> 12s for accepts.

Emma: Symptoms: elevated accept queue on replicas, connection spikes. Trying quick triage: is this a traffic spike or backend leak?

Kai: I see a burst of long-poll inference reads from a small set of clients around 00:18 UTC. Possibly warmup traffic from a customer rollout. Also PG connection backpressure correlates with same timeframe.

Tara: Confirmed — onboarding job kicked off heavy evaluation runs at ~00:16, lots of streaming requests. ETA to throttle on customer's side unknown.

Emma: Immediate mitigations: 1) enable read-only fallback for non-critical traffic, 2) temporarily increase pgbouncer pool for read paths, 3) throttle or rate-limit the offending app routes via gateway. Doing 1 & 2 now.

Emma: Applying pgbouncer bump:
```
ssh gateway-ops
sudo kubectl -n infra edit configmap pgbouncer-config
# set pool_size_read = 500 -> 800 for cluster-wide
```

Miguel: Heads up: increasing pool_size will raise DB connections, watch pg maxconn. I'll watch PG metrics.

prod-monitor-bot: pgbouncer config update applied (rollout started). New pool target observed at 00:22 UTC.

Emma: Also reduced accept rate to replicas by enabling a short-lived routing rule: route streaming inference to fallback read cache for 60s for high-rate clients. Applied via router: `route set high-rate -> read-cache`.

Kai: While those are rolling, I want to reduce open sockets to Redis on replicas. Proposed: temporarily lower `maxclients` via redis.conf (safe drop), and trigger a staggered restart of replicas to clear stuck accepts. Risks: transient errors for active requests. Thoughts?

Tara: Do staggered restarts (one replica at a time), with drain first. We should shift traffic off a replica before bump. Use health check toggles.

Emma: Starting drain on r3.

prod-monitor-bot: r3: drain initiated. Connection count decreasing. accept_queue_r3 -> 48.

Emma: Restarting r3 now (`kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis-repl-r3 -n infra`).

Kai: Restart complete. r3 back up, accept_queue_r3 ~15, latency back to ~0.12s for r3. Good.

Emma: Rolling r2 now (drain -> restart).

Miguel: Watch replication lag before failover. If lag > 30s hold. Also coordinating with PG team on read-replica load because we've shifted load.

prod-monitor-bot: r2 restart done. r2 healthy. r1 remains slightly elevated at accept_queue ~320.

Tara: r1 still hot. Is there a single client causing most connections?

Emma: Looking at connection origins: 83% from a handful of IPs associated to `customer-alpha` app tokens. I pinged the solutions contact to tell them to throttle.

Emma: Customer contact replied: they've paused the batch job. We'll see drop.

prod-monitor-bot: within 60s of pause, cluster accept_queue avg -> 72, p50 latency -> 0.18s, errors -> decreased.

pagerduty: Update: Emma acknowledged at 1791234569, incident active.

Kai: Post-mitigation: suggested config follow-ups: - enable per-client connection limits via `client-output-buffer-limit` tuning, - set `client-query-buffer-limit`, - add reject-on-throttle on our gateway for streaming endpoints, - improve early-shed logic in inference proxy.

Tara: Also recommend a short-term autoscaling rule for replicas accept capacity and a playbook entry for staged restarts. Will raise PR.

Emma: Customer impact: partial. Some streaming inference requests timed out during peak (error rate spike to 1.9% for ~6 minutes). Non-streaming short requests unaffected. No broad data loss. Notified CS and support to surface to affected customers.

Miguel: Running a quick post-check for error logs and timeouts. Searching: `grep -i "ERR max clients" /var/log/redis/*` -> few entries on r1 during peak.

Emma: Coordinating handoff. I'll keep incident open for 15m post-stable then hand to follow-up owner. Next steps: 
- Tara to open PR for gateway throttle and playbook edits.
- Kai to propose redis conf hardening and staging restarts doc.
- Miguel to run load test to validate pgbouncer and PG headroom.
- Emma to file incident note and link metrics.

prod-monitor-bot: cluster stable for 7m. accept_queue_avg < 40. No new alerts in the last 3m.

Emma: PD: running a brief post-incident check. If all good, will resolve in 10m and hand to follow-up owners.

Tara: FYI — adding to backlog: implement per-customer rate limits on evaluation API and improve routing to avoid overloading replicas.

Miguel: I'll schedule a chaos rehearsal for the restart procedure next week.

Emma: Marking handoff in 10. Reassigning follow-ups: Tara (gateway throttle + playbook), Kai (redis config + restart doc), Miguel (DB/pgbouncer load test).

pagerduty: Incident PD-87421 status: acknowledged -> resolved at 1791234630 by Emma.

Emma: Resolving thread. Final notes: root cause = sudden customer-generated streaming burst that exceeded replica accept capacity; mitigations: routing/rate-limit and staggered replica restarts; follow-ups assigned. Posting incident writeup to #postmortems tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
